consensus_summary: Symbolically, the bill of divorcement primarily represents God's judicial covenant severance from unfaithful Israel (spiritual adultery/idolatry), expressed as exile, within the prophetic marriage metaphor (with restoration often in view); the term is also frequently literal/ethical.
book_summary: The covenant lawsuit executed as the wife sent out of the house (exile and scattering); hated when it betrays the covenant wife, but commanded when the union is fornication (a marriage God never joined); God gave Israel the bill and answered His own no-return rule at the cross.
consensus_core_identification: God's judicial divorce/separation of unfaithful Israel for spiritual adultery, resulting in exile/judgment under the husband-wife covenant metaphor.
book_core_identification: Executed covenant lawsuit sending the wife out (exile/scattering of Israel), with the additional framing that divorce is hated for true covenant wives but commanded for illegitimate unions, plus resolution of Deut 24's no-return via the cross.
boundary_disagreement: Book adds the hated-vs-commanded distinction (applying to covenant betrayal vs. fornication/unions God never joined, e.g. foreign wives) and explicitly includes the cross as answering/resolving the Deuteronomy 24 no-return prohibition after God's divorce of Israel.
material_contradiction: None; the book's core of Israel's divorce-as-exile matches the consensus primary without denying it.
rationale: Minimum cores identify the same central referent (prophetic bill of divorcement as God's covenant lawsuit/exile of unfaithful Israel). Extra details do not create artificial disagreement. The book preserves that referent while broadening extension and precision with the hated/commanded boundary conditions and the cross resolution of the no-return rule (a recognizable but minority alternative in consensus). This is boundary refinement, not core replacement.
strongest_objection: The cross answering the no-return rule (and full integration of commanded divorce for 'fornication' unions) elevates a minority legal-typological reading into the entry's core statement, beyond the settled consensus primary of simple covenant judgment/exile.
